sources.entry: Websoft9 ⚠ - GitOps-driven, multi-application hosting for cloud servers and home servers, one-click deployment of 200+ open source apps. (Demo, Source Code, Clients) LGPL-3.0 Shell/Python

summary.one_liner: Websoft9 is a self-hosted, web-based PaaS for deploying and managing 300+ open source applications on a single server without Kubernetes.
summary.what_it_does: Provides a web console acting as a private app store where you can one-click install open source apps such as WordPress, GitLab, and Mattermost. Once installed, apps can be started, stopped, restarted, redeployed, have logs viewed, and have files and volumes managed from the console. It also includes a web file manager, a browser-based SSH terminal, and domain binding with free Let's Encrypt SSL certificates via Nginx Proxy Manager. Other features listed are scheduled local backups for apps and databases, a GUI for custom docker-compose stacks, multi-user accounts with role-based access, and real-time host monitoring with a log viewer. It runs as a single Docker container that bundles AppHub (Python/FastAPI), a React/TypeScript console, Portainer, and Nginx Proxy Manager, managed by supervisord.
use_cases: Self-host WordPress or GitLab on one server
One-click install of open source apps
Manage domains and SSL certificates for self-hosted apps
Schedule backups of app data and databases
Deploy custom docker-compose stacks through a web GUI
Manage files and terminal access on a remote server from a browser
how_to_run: Open port 9000 in a browser (or the --console-port you set) and follow the setup wizard
sudo bash uninstall.sh --purge (removes everything including data)
notable: Runs as a single Docker container bundling API, UI, orchestration, and reverse proxy, with no Kubernetes required
One-click app catalog of 300+ open source applications
Dry-run pre-flight check option (--dry-run) before installing
Built-in web file manager and browser SSH terminal
Free Let's Encrypt SSL via Nginx Proxy Manager
caveats: Install script is wget-piped and runs as root with sudo, so review it before running
README includes an additional restriction: publishing images based on this repo to cloud marketplaces without authorization is prohibited, so it is not fully LGPL-free for that use
Cloud marketplace listings are described as certified with business support, implying a commercial offering alongside the open source project
